sections.section_title: Initial Presentation and the Clinical Recognition of Anaphylaxis
sections.description: This section introduces the fundamental concepts of anaphylaxis and applies them to the patient's initial emergency department presentation. It focuses on the immediate identification of a life-threatening allergic reaction and the role of drug triggers.
subtopics: Definition and clinical criteria for anaphylaxis
Pharmacological triggers: The role of macrolides (Clarithromycin) and cross-reactivity considerations
Analyzing the initial presentation: Hemodynamic instability (hypotension), respiratory distress (hypoxemia), and cutaneous manifestations
Immediate stabilization: Airway, breathing, and circulation (ABC) priorities in the ED

sections.section_title: The Spectrum of Anaphylactic Courses: Biphasic and Multiphasic Reactions
sections.description: This section explores the temporal patterns of anaphylaxis, distinguishing between a single episode, biphasic reactions, and the rare multiphasic course seen in this case. It examines the challenges of monitoring and ICU admission for recurrent shock.
subtopics: Defining biphasic vs. multiphasic anaphylaxis
Differentiating true biphasic reactions from refractory anaphylaxis and ongoing allergen absorption
Clinical progression: Analyzing the patient's four distinct episodes of shock
Monitoring protocols: The debate over observation duration and risk stratification for relapse
ICU management and the necessity of continuous monitoring in multiphasic cases

sections.description: This section details the treatment of anaphylaxis, focusing on the nuances of dosing and the current shift in the evidence regarding adjunctive therapies like corticosteroids.
subtopics: Epinephrine dosing: The clinical significance of 0.3mg vs. 0.5mg and weight-based dosing (0.01 mg/kg)
The role of epinephrine auto-injectors in clinical and pre-clinical settings
Adjunctive therapies: H1-antihistamines (Clemastine) and fluid resuscitation
Critical appraisal of corticosteroids: Reviewing the evidence against their use in preventing biphasic reactions
Alternative advanced strategies: Continuous intravenous epinephrine pumps vs. expectant management

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Reasoning: Biomarkers and Tryptase Kinetics
sections.description: This section explains how to move from clinical symptoms to a biochemical diagnosis, focusing on the use and timing of serum tryptase to identify mast cell activation.
subtopics: Pathophysiology of mast cell activation and mediator release
Serum tryptase: The 'gold standard' biomarker for anaphylaxis
The critical window for tryptase sampling: Baseline vs. peak (1-4 hours) vs. resolution (24+ hours)
Interpreting abnormal tryptase levels and the impact of delayed sampling in this case

sections.section_title: Underlying Pathology: Systemic Mastocytosis and Long-Term Care
sections.description: This section delves into the underlying cause of this patient's severe reactions, explaining systemic mastocytosis and the comprehensive approach to long-term patient safety.
subtopics: Pathophysiology of Systemic Mastocytosis: Mast cell proliferation and hyper-responsiveness
WHO diagnostic criteria for systemic mastocytosis (Major and Minor criteria)
Extramastocytic manifestations: Hepatomegaly and neuropsychiatric symptoms (depression, memory loss)
Long-term management: Allergen avoidance, maintenance antihistamines, and patient education on auto-injector use
